### Lane B — every chip in the bar's machine cluster does one named thing, and Settings reaches Home's garden

`active` · `@legeos.work.bar-cluster-clickable-20260908/1` · part of `@legeos.milestone.developer-edition-0-1/1`

The user's report on the installed session at gfbe4480 was that the bar's bottom-right buttons are not clickable, that network should open nm-tray-2, that the separate power/battery bar should become a full OS Settings button, that date/time should open an existing calendar rather than a new one, and that the furthest bottom-right button was unlabelled and frightening. Finding 6 of the Homegarden usability review adds that Settings excludes every `shell.home-garden.*` key, so default-on automation has no graphical settings.

Three of those were literal: the readings chip and the clock had no click handler at all, so a click on either fell through to the bar's own ground and merely re-activated the window. The fourth was worse than literal: the network chip *was* wired, but `app.rs::network_control_app` resolved the control by desktop-file name (`*nm-tray.desktop`) while the action `network.open-control` has always declared `Requires::Provider(ProviderRole::NetworkStatusUi)`. On this host `lege providers` prints `network-status-ui  no application declares this role` and the registry nonetheless holds `desktop-import.nm-tray.desktop` for Ubuntu's stock nm-tray 0.5.1 — which ignores `--popup`, only ever draws a tray icon, and had no tray to draw into. The chip lit up and launched something invisible.

The work: the cluster becomes account · clock · network · Settings, right to left, with the readings moved into the account popover's first line and their 112 pixels spent on a Settings chip; the account chip wears the account's name beside its mark; the confirm rows read "Click again to log out"; the clock gains `clock.open-calendar`, which resolves the first application declaring `Categories=Calendar` (gsimplecal preferred, and now in the desktop seed); the network chip resolves the provider role and nothing else; and Settings gains a Homegarden tab with the typed `shell.home-garden.*` keys, an editable ignore list and the hidden places from `HomeGarden1.Contexts`, each with an Unhide that calls `Hide(path, false)`.

### A new window takes the keyboard at map, and Alt+Tab walks every window on a list frozen for the hold

`active` · `@legeos.work.focus-and-switching-20260908/1` · part of `@legeos.milestone.developer-edition-0-1/1`

Lane A of campaign 4, from the user's session at gfbe4480: an application opened from the Home search bar maps unfocused under a Home surface that still holds the keyboard, and Alt+Tab cannot reach a window buried under two others. Three parts. (1) WindowService::should_activate_on_map — a client window, and no visible activated fullscreen client window on the same output — is called from both map paths (xdg_shell::handle_toplevel_commit after apply_surface_claims, xwayland::map_window_request) so a newly mapped window takes the keyboard; nothing else in the map sequence activates one and a launch through Launcher1 carries no xdg-activation token. (2) The switcher walks a list frozen at the first press (lege_window::SwitchRing) until the modifier is released: every step activates, activation raises, and the list is the stacking order, so a list rebuilt per press only ever swaps the top two windows and a third window was unreachable however many times Tab was pressed. Alt+Tab now walks every unshelved client window in most-recently-activated order — which the stacking order already is, LayerStack's rank being a monotonic counter bumped on every raise, so there is deliberately no recency stamp on WindowRecord. Within-group cycling is dropped: scoping Alt+Tab to the focused window's group made a group a place Alt+Tab could not leave. Super+Tab is unchanged in meaning and gains the same frozen list. cycle_focus, cycle_within_group and cycle_groups are deleted. (3) taskbar::entries was found to lose no window; the remaining bar gap is that a multi-window application chip shows no count, sent to the coordinator as a bar_screen.rs hunk (Lane B's file).

### Homegarden Phases 0–3: the activity ledger and Garden Clock, the tender, tending at reveal and session start, and the rung-aware Place tile

`active` · `@legeos.work.homegarden-phases-0-3/1` · part of `@legeos.milestone.developer-edition-0-1/1`

Build the Homegarden model far enough to judge it in a day's use (@legeos.decision.homegarden-activity-grown-places, docs/garden/*.md): (1) a pure ledger in lege-session-core with HomeActivity/HomeContext, weights bucketed per (kind, role, session) so breadth beats count, root attribution behind a RootProbe (project root, existing context, workspace marker, mount point, XDG user dir; never $HOME), an ignore list as a setting, a bounded activity tree (depth 3, 32 nodes), stages Dormant/Trace/Tile/Expanded with promotion by relevance+sessions+breadth and demotion only when later sessions AND garden-hours both pass, and a Garden Clock that advances at Lifecycle1's session edges and never on wall-clock; (2) a pure tender in lege-field (garden::tend) emitting Place/Resize/Remove with a reason each, never Move, a Place only on free cells, a Resize only when nothing but an unpinned un-user-sized garden tile yields, property-tested; (3) org.legeos.HomeGarden1 on sessiond (Observe/Tend/Contexts/Describe/Pin/Hide/Forget/ForgetAll/Clock, signal Tended) applying each tending as one HomeField1 batch, recorded in History1, with sources: the launch channel (directory arguments -> LaunchedHere with the app's role), the shell's brokered open (FileOpened), the session-edge channel (the clock); (4) the shell tends at session start and on every Home reveal edge, draws a grown Folder tile by rung (Small: name + state; Wide: + roles row of text-led tools; Large: + the branch body of used structure, heavier branches thicker, falling back to the listing), and offers place.open-* and garden.* through the one action manifest (context menu, cheat sheet, lege garden CLI). Settings shell.home-garden.* hold the levers; default on.

### Act on the Homegarden usability review: the view takes every remote change, the user's tiles are the user's, growth never shifts a neighbour, the garden verbs do what they say, a corner landing leaves room to grow

`active` · `@legeos.work.homegarden-review-fixes-20260908/1` · part of `@legeos.milestone.developer-edition-0-1/1`

The six findings of @legeos.assessment.homegarden-usability-review-20260908, five here and the sixth (a Settings Homegarden page) in @legeos.work.bar-cluster-clickable-20260908. (1) The shell reconciles the daemon's field on HomeField1.Changed: adopt, resize in place, remove folder tiles (field_model::reconcile_remote). (2) A folder tile the tender never placed is the user's outright: at the next tending it is pinned and kept (user_span = its span), so recession neither resizes nor removes it. (3) The tender rejects any resize whose yields shift a neighbour's cell, trying each axis alone before emitting nothing (lege-field::garden::plan_resize). (4) garden.keep is HomeGarden1.Keep (pin + freeze the size); Hide unpins and removes the tile from every Home now, undoably; Forget drops the record and removes the tile likewise; the context menu offers Pin or Unpin by the place's state and Keep only until kept. (5) A first landing takes the home corner as a 4x3 would sit in it (GROWTH_ROOM), so a Trace can become Expanded in place.

### Home holds only your own things — the file manager works, running windows and the machine's instruments leave Home

`proposed` · `@legeos.work.home-purity-20260908/1` · part of `@legeos.milestone.developer-edition-0-1/1`

A hands-on run of the installed session on 2026-09-08 found the file manager doing nothing from Home, unselectable in Settings, and absent from the launcher under its own name; and found Home crowded with things that are not the user's own — a tile per running window, a container tile per window group, a Session, a Notifications and a Settings tile, a plate labelled "Home" standing on Home, and a permanent Help button. docs/garden/garden.md draws the line this work applies: Home deals with your stuff, the bar deals with the machine.

Four root causes, all read off the source rather than guessed. (1) The shell fetched only the `terminal` and `file-search` provider roles, so `providers[FileManager]` was never filled and every folder press took `open_in_file_manager`'s "no file manager is selected" branch on a session that had one selected. (2) The Files object's tile still launched `org.legeos.Files` by name — an application this desktop no longer ships — instead of routing through the role. (3) `derive_manifest` parsed `OnlyShowIn`/`NotShowIn` and threw them away, so `/etc/xdg/autostart/lxqt-desktop.desktop` (`OnlyShowIn=LXQt`, running `pcmanfm-qt --desktop`) won the default-variant election and the launcher's only row for PCManFM-Qt was named "Desktop" and painted a desktop. (4) The provider chooser's label was "name (import id) · priority N" in a 300px field, which elided inside the parenthesis and told the reader neither which application it was nor what its priority was.

And the subtraction: `merge_sessions` and `merge_window_groups` placed a tile for every running window and every group; `merge_system` placed the three machine widgets and `merge_panels` grouped them into a shelf. All are deleted. The merge's existing sweep removes what a saved field still carries, with no migration of its own — `wanted` never names a window tile — and one `migrate_system_tiles` takes off all seven retired system probes as ordinary invertible `Remove` ops.

### Planning: a COSMIC-derived popup window manager, uninterrupted fullscreen, and functional edge tabs

`proposed` · `@legeos.work.window-manager-popup-and-functional-edge-tabs/1` · part of `@legeos.milestone.developer-edition-0-1/1`

Planning only, following the user's 2026-09-08 request: the taskbar must not show in fullscreen; a popup window manager must reuse cosmic-applets code; retain and refine LegeOS's own compact, functional design language, eliminating redundancy gradually. No implementation, dependency import, deployment or live-session operation is authorized by this record. The explicit fullscreen/no-peek and COSMIC-code direction is accepted in @legeos.decision.one-persistent-bottom-bar-tags-not-bands/3. The interaction, composition and sizing choices below are recommendations to review.

PRODUCT MODEL. Home owns places and launching. Attached window tags identify and manipulate the current visible windows. Windows is one on-demand inventory of running work, including parked and fullscreen windows. Machine controls own system state. A permanent repeated row of app logos/window titles adds little when the window already has its own tag. Remove that row only once the replacement manager makes every parked or obscured window reachable. Grouping remains explicit and compositor-owned; app identity alone may organize a display list but never creates a LegeOS group.

FULLSCREEN. Every ordinary managed toplevel should have a compositor-level Fullscreen action via its tag's existing management affordance and the popup, plus a proposed Super+F binding after conflict checks. Support native Wayland and XWayland; fixed-size clients retain a safe centered surface if they cannot render at the requested size. Owned dialogs must remain reachable above their parent. Entering fullscreen preserves geometry, output, maximize state, group membership and stacking context. Selecting another window suspends presentation of the old fullscreen window without changing its fullscreen flag, parking it or losing its restore slot; returning presents it fullscreen again. Selecting ordinary work restores the ordinary arrangement. This is a per-output presentation choice in the existing one-workspace model; no macOS Spaces or inferred groups are introduced. Focus changing to a different monitor does not hide the fullscreen app on the first. Leaving fullscreen restores prior ordinary/fit state. Plain Escape remains application-owned except when the manager itself is open; Ctrl+Alt+Escape remains compositor recovery. No bar, clock, tabs, invisible pointer strip or bar pixels through transparency while fullscreen is presented. Hover and bottom-edge dwell do nothing to shell chrome. An explicit Home command changes to the Home view while retaining the saved fullscreen state; this is distinct from overlaying the bar on fullscreen.

POPUP. One compact, opaque, content-sized surface, anchored at the lower-left of the invoking output, above both ordinary and fullscreen clients but below security/permission/recovery surfaces. It reserves no work area and opens without moving/resizing windows. Proposed invocation: click Windows at the normal edge; Super+W globally; Super+secondary-click as a deliberate pointer gesture anywhere, including fullscreen. The pointer gesture and chord are proposals, not settled preferences. They must not conflict with window dragging/grouping or flash Home through bare-Super handling. Preserve current Alt+Tab within group and Super+Tab across groups; fast cycling stays compositor-owned. The manager is a latched inspect/act view, not a mandatory delay on each switch. If a mouse-only fullscreen route is required, choose an explicit edge gesture that opens only the manager and never an automatic hover reveal; evaluate it in the interaction trial before assigning a hotspot.

POPUP CONTENT. One row per window, with explicit groups shown once and expandable in place; title first, small app identity only where it disambiguates, state text only for Parked, Fullscreen, or another output. Avoid simultaneous duplicate all/group/app lists and avoid a second app launcher. Group entry activates its last-active member, preserving relationships; an individual member has its own actions. A single selected/hovered-window preview uses the existing trusted preview path, requested only while the popup needs it. This lets two identical terminal titles be distinguished without a permanent thumbnail for every row. List rows remain usable if capture fails; display a named placeholder or unavailable state, never a fabricated live image. Keep insertion order stable while the popup is open; seed selection from recent focus, hold it by WindowId, append new arrivals without moving the target under the pointer, remove closed windows without activating their replacement. Keyboard arrows navigate, Enter activates/restores, Escape/outside click cancels and restores the prior focus. Pointer activation is one click; focus/hover only previews. Closed-while-open, rename, same-app multiple windows, and unavailable title/icon are normal states. Type-to-filter is local to open windows, never the Home launcher; clear query when dismissed. Use a bounded scrolling list only when content demands it. Selected-window actions: Fit / Restore, Fullscreen / Leave fullscreen, Park / Restore parked, Close, and contextual Group/Ungroup. Expose the appropriate state-dependent actions, not conflicting pairs. Close asks the client to close and lets its unsaved-work dialog decide; it must never become forced process termination. Reuse the same target/action declarations for a tag-opened manager scoped to that window.

NON-FULLSCREEN EDGE. Recommended resting composition: Home and a single Windows tab at the left; a compact time/machine tab at the right; no full-width painted panel and no always-visible per-app inventory. Windows appears when any window exists, including when all are parked; zero windows leaves Home and machine access. Its label may show total window count only if the trial finds it useful, otherwise a readable Windows label suffices. Keep a stable corner and ordering rather than hiding individual entries as overlap/focus changes. The right tab displays time and useful power state; network/volume details live in its popup unless an actionable condition makes an indicator worth exposing (disconnect, mute, low charge). This does not make controls disappear: machine controls remain available at a stable target and via existing hardware/chord routes. Home should not gain a duplicate Settings/Help/Session plate.

GEOMETRY AND MATERIAL. Carry forward current tag geometry and ink, modest corner radii, existing theme palette and group accent grammar. Prototype one 32-logical-pixel tag-height seam instead of the current 48px bar: smaller painted objects do not justify tiny hit targets. Preserve an adequate target under pointer/touch scaling. Fit/maximized windows use that same seam for their single title/control set; do not add a second title row or repeated maximize controls. A normal fitted application needs a safe rectangular area so edge controls do not cover its content; the tag-height reservation is a deliberate usability cost, not an invisible 48px leftover. Fullscreen uses all output pixels. Keep left and right surfaces separate (or use a tested alpha-capable path with accurate input regions) so unpainted space is not an opaque bar; current softbuffer XRGB cannot supply transparency. Opening a popup adds no exclusive-zone height and changes no application geometry. Empty space between windows belongs to work/Home and needs no decorative filler.

VISUAL LANGUAGE. A boundary denotes something separable or manipulable; a tag is an attachment to its owner; a raised surface denotes a temporary decision. Material distinguishes object kind using existing palette roles. Accent retains group identity with a textual/grouping cue; focus uses one clear outline/ink treatment rather than another competing color system. State has one small cue, with readable names on focus or inspection. Do not add generic OS branding, giant cards, ornamental blur, duplicate badges, mirrored clocks, desktop miniatures or a permanent account portrait. Functional space includes separation for reading, dragging and avoiding accidental activation. Eliminate repeated information before reducing text sizes, targets or meaningful spacing. Pointer routes and keyboard accelerators are complementary access, not redundancy to remove.

CODE REUSE. Inspected pop-os/cosmic-applets commit 1aa03111c5cd92051c9af28b43cb1ee9f43dbb25 (2026-09-01). Primary donor: cosmic-app-list/src/app.rs popup lifecycle, toplevel reconciliation and selected-window preview/action behavior; wayland_subscription.rs provides an explicit request/update separation and Screencopy request. Supplement: cosmic-applet-minimize/src/lib.rs and window_image.rs for parked-window/overflow/preview handling. Reuse/adapt actual selected source with file-level upstream SHA, copyright/SPDX notices and a documented local delta, not merely copy COSMIC's visual appearance or claim another independent rewrite is code reuse. The existing bar says its COSMIC behavior was reimplemented, so it does not already satisfy this new reuse request. The donor is a libcosmic/cctk applet, not a drop-in LegeOS widget: map upstream toplevel handles to WindowId, messages to the trusted lege_shell bridge, image requests to existing LegeOS capture, and desktop identity to appd; render in the established Pixelkit language. Do not bring COSMIC's compositor, panel hosting, workspace authority or another background window inventory just to host the popup. Begin with a narrow extraction/proof-of-fit and record which source was retained. Upstream ToplevelRequest exposes Activate, Minimize and Quit, not the required fullscreen control, so fullscreen is a LegeOS compositor/bridge addition. The existing all-ShellOverlay peek exception must be replaced by visibility/composition rules for the bar and a narrowly authorized manager surface. Preserving an inactive window's fullscreen state additionally needs a presentation policy, because current stacking promotes every unshelved fullscreen window regardless of activation.

GRADUAL CUTOVER. (1) Establish actual donor/adaptor seam and a tested window-state/action model. (2) Add compositor-controlled fullscreen entry, distinct presentation selection, bar exclusion and explicit manager invocation while preserving existing recovery. (3) Add popup coverage for every running/parked/grouped/fullscreen window, keyboard/pointer operation, preview fallback and scoped actions. (4) Replace per-app bar chips/hover row with the Windows entry; consolidate status/account controls and fit-window controls into the single seam. Delete redundant paths only after the replacement's acceptance passes, without shipping a permanent choice between two inventories. (5) Trial daily work and refine labels/counts, preview density, pointer invocation and seam geometry. No broad refactor or desktop replacement is implied.

PLANNING ARTIFACT. The retained conversation study .agent/scratch/window-manager-plan-20260908/window-manager-states.html compares ordinary windows, uninterrupted fullscreen and the explicit manager over fullscreen. It is an interaction sketch, not a finished UI, production implementation or pixel-perfect acceptance baseline.

### Home Field widget foundations — neighbour-yielding resize, the widget contract, the action manifest, and Lifecycle1 as the service pattern

`active` · `@legeos.work.home-widget-foundations/3` · part of `@legeos.milestone.m2-session-runs/1`

The Home Field was a dead end for a desktop tester: no way to launch anything, no logout/restart/shutdown, no way to close a window, and a search bar that does nothing outside an expanded drawer. The decision is that every missing capability arrives as a widget on the one screen rather than as a panel or tray, consistent with M2's taskbar-free commitment. This item builds only the foundation those widgets stand on, in four parts. (1) A resize that lets adjacent tiles give up span instead of being evicted: reflow::find_resize, where a yielding neighbour keeps its far edge and the request is clamped to the largest span every neighbour can absorb. (2) The widget contract over TileKind::System, which was a designed-for slot nothing constructed: a descriptor declares what shows at each representation rung and which regions are clickable, and each region names an action rather than coding a behaviour. (3) An action manifest in lege-types, so one declaration drives the shell's labels, the keyboard accelerator and the lege verb. (4) org.legeos.Session.Lifecycle1 on sessiond forwarding to logind, built as the one worked example of the service-interface pattern every future widget follows.

### Home Field widgets — every missing desktop capability as a tile on the one screen

`proposed` · `@legeos.work.home-widgets/1` · part of `@legeos.milestone.m2-session-runs/1`

A gap review of the Home Field against what any desktop of the last twenty years offers found that a cold session gives the user eight drawer tiles and the message "open an application and it will appear", with no way to open one. Application tiles are derived only from windows that are already running and are removed when the last one closes, so the launcher route is circular. There is no logout, restart, shutdown, suspend or lock; no way to close a window; no volume, brightness or battery; no notification rendering despite sessiond hosting the notification server; no context menus; and the field's own search bar does nothing outside an expanded drawer. The decision is that each of these arrives as a widget on the single screen — information first, sub-clickable, opening a window only as a deliberate second step — rather than as a panel, a dock or a tray, which is consistent with M2's taskbar-free commitment and with homefield.md's rule that the launcher is inventory and the home screen is working memory. @legeos.work.home-widget-foundations built the framework; this item is the umbrella for the widgets themselves and for the window controls that are still missing.

## [Integrated design roadmap — Home, Files, perimeter resize, event services and Developer Edition storage](ACTIVE-WORK.md#integrated-design-roadmap--home-files-perimeter-resize-event-services-and-developer-edition-storage) `@legeos.work.design-consolidation-roadmap/1`

### WS6 — build identity, local archive, lege dev deploy, compatibility gates, and replay-gated resourced improvements

`active` · `@legeos.work.deployment-activation-and-resourced/1` · part of `@legeos.work.design-consolidation-roadmap/1`

Tracks A-E, landing order A1 A2 A3 A4 B1 B2 B3 E0 C1 C2 B4 E1 E5 E6 D1 D2 E2 E3 E4 C3. Track A: BuildSetId is the Debian version (0.1.0~dev<epoch>+g<sha7>[.dirty]) across all 13 packages via cargo xtask build-set, which rejects mixed sets; every long-lived process writes a runtime build stamp file at startup (filesystem-first because comp and shell serve no D-Bus; not RuntimeDirectory=, which would delete siblings' stamps); distro/deploy/components.toml is the machine-readable component matrix; lege dev status computes installed-versus-running convergence; doctor gains BuildSetCoherent and RunningMatchesInstalled with PackageAgesConsistent as the documented fallback. Track B: a local signed APT repo at /var/lib/legeos/devrepo (apt-ftparchive + per-developer gpg key, keep=3 sets), one transactional apt-get install --allow-downgrades per set, lege dev rollback as the same path, and an activation engine with per-component rules — shell restart with health gate, apps at next launch, resourced controlled restart, sessiond/filed/portal only when the compatibility gates pass (shipped manual until the composed-session restart test exists), hostd blocked mid-transaction, compositor always needs-session, kernel/boot needs-reboot — ending in the convergence report with the previous set retained. Track C: xtask interface-baseline/check-interface-signatures turns the frozen-signature convention into an enforced gate; lege-state gains schema_meta with min_reader_version, an open()-time refusal of too-new databases, VACUUM INTO snapshots, and the documented one-rollback-generation policy; lege-field gains a document migration registry applied at the load boundary with DocumentTooNew never overwriting. Track D: lege-boot-health calls MarkGood/Rollback itself, and hostd's reconcile_boot wires the GRUB tries counter; cryptographic verification and the hardware matrix stay explicitly deferred. Track E, all gated behind the E0 replay harness (replay recorded traces through Governor::decide with a round-trip fidelity test): thresholds scale with MemTotal (reserve clamp 6.25% 768MiB-4GiB, critical clamp 2% 256MiB-1.5GiB, reproducing today's constants at 48GiB), unsaved-work gains a producer and a TTL via additive SetInstanceWork, richer safe-to-sacrifice signals via additive SetInstanceActivity (idle age, project importance, checkpoint freshness reaching scoring for the first time, user pin as strong weight never hard exclusion), Governor::plan returns multi-step reclaim plans (Elevated trims up to three, Severe throttles top-K to the deficit, Critical stays single-victim) with the foreground structurally excluded at Severe unless demonstrably the runaway, protect.rs stops lowering memory.low and covers sessiond and filed, and ADR-0014 settles systemd-oomd ownership (armed backstop on app.slice at 90%, off on session.slice, avoid on the five session units).

### Next Home usability sequence — adaptable Home, complete folder surfaces, then common Settings

`active` · `@legeos.work.home-surface-usability-next/1` · part of `@legeos.work.home-field/2`

Carry the Home surface from a fixed demonstration layout to an ordinary daily desktop in the order set by the user on 2026-08-31.

First, make Home itself adaptable: configurable Home-only panels/rails/docks, automatic panel layouts for different output shapes, user-invoked arrangements for all open windows, and immediate reversible switching among those arrangements. Preserve truly chrome-free fullscreen application work and refine bare Super from release-only toggling into immediate press/hold Home reveal with shortcut-safe semantics.

Second, make folders and composite shortcut panes the Home file objects. Build copy/cut/paste, drag and drop, delete/trash and the remaining ordinary file verbs on the multi-selection foundation; then add deterministic sorting and list-versus-thumbnail presentation. Loose individual file tiles are explicitly not part of this model.

Third, make the graphical Settings app adjust the common controls a person expects: resolution/refresh/rotation/scale, mouse and trackpad behaviour, and appearance/theme/material choices. Accessibility remains deferred behind these product-completeness items per the user's standing priority.

### Interim application integration — the Terminal role and the Super+grave drop-down terminal, the Files context menu, the search panel with FSearch as the FileSearch provider, Kitty defaults

`active` · `@legeos.work.application-integration-interim/2` · part of `@legeos.work.home-surface-usability-next/1`

Integration choices the user made on 2026-09-03, revised later the same day. (a) Terminal: ProviderRole::Terminal, exclusive, candidates from TerminalEmulator desktop entries, default kitty; the shell relays the selection with lege_shell_manager_v1.set_terminal and answers terminal_requested by launching the provider through the launch chain; Super+grave (compositor chord; a bare ~ or ` is a typed character and cannot be a global chord) toggles the terminal: launch when none, unshelve/activate when shelved or unfocused, shelve and refocus the previous window when focused, never close. No Ctrl+Alt+T. 'Open terminal here' in the Files context menu launches it with --directory. /etc/xdg/kitty/kitty.conf shipped by legeos-shell with the LegeOS palette, background_opacity 0.85, remember_window_size no, wayland_titlebar_color system, overridable by ~/.config/kitty. (b) Files object: secondary-click menu on rows and empty space reusing surface/context_menu.rs and the declared files.* verbs (Open, Open with…, Open terminal here, Copy path, Rename, Move to trash, Properties; New folder, Paste, Select all, Sort by…, Show hidden), then multi-select, keyboard verbs, drag-and-drop and properties-as-pane. (c) Search: the top field on Home stays the application launcher only (COSMIC's launcher shape); real search is the Files object's search field expanded into a partial-screen panel (about two thirds of the field, centred, hairline edge) over lege-filed's scoped index with path, size and modified time per row and keyboard navigation, whose last row is 'Search everywhere with FSearch'; ProviderRole::FileSearch, exclusive, launched with --search <query>; 'Search here…' in the context menu. The later indexing direction replaces the interim two-database arrangement: lege-filed owns one persistent, incrementally maintained derived file index used by integrated Files search, a remote-index FSearch fork, Silvaview-rs, the CLI and future clients.

### Graphical Settings for displays, mouse/trackpad and Home appearance

`active` · `@legeos.work.home-field-settings-gui/1` · part of `@legeos.work.home-surface-usability-next/1`

The graphical Settings app already edits the five Home Field tuning keys; replace the vague goal of making every read-only diagnostic tab editable with the common controls needed for daily use.

Displays: enumerate connected outputs and allow resolution, refresh rate, rotation/orientation and scale per output, including mixed-scale arrangements. Apply through compositor-owned validated configuration with a visible confirmation countdown and automatic rollback when the new mode is not confirmed or the output disappears. Show the resulting logical arrangement before applying and retain a known-good configuration.

Mouse and trackpad: expose pointer speed, acceleration profile, natural scrolling, primary-button choice and scroll behaviour; for touchpads also tap-to-click, tap-and-drag, two-finger/edge scrolling and disable-while-typing where libinput supports them. Unsupported controls are identified as unavailable rather than drawn as inert switches.

Appearance: select light/dark or bundled themes, accent and object-material palette/texture roles, background/wallpaper behaviour, and the defaults used by Home panels, folder panes and widgets. Themes are declarative design tokens/material assets, never executable shell extensions, and application fullscreen remains free of Home chrome. Every graphical setting writes through a typed service/schema and has Reset; CLI inspection/change remains equivalent. Provider, association, history and hardware diagnostic pages may remain read-only until their own scoped work exists.

### Lane A — compositor: bottom tags replace the title band, the corner grip goes, a maximized window under the bar has no frame

`active` · `@legeos.work.window-tags-replace-the-band/2` · part of `@legeos.work.home-surface-usability-next/1`

lege-window: RECOVERY_BAND_HEIGHT becomes TAG_HEIGHT and recovery_band becomes tag_strip, the full-width strip at a window's bottom edge; client_area/frame_around keep the origin and differ by one strip height; repair_window clamps so the bottom strip stays on an output (a tall window hangs off the top); move_into_view sets a too-tall window flush with the bottom edge; resize_grip and RESIZE_GRIP_SIZE are deleted and MIN_WINDOW_HEIGHT is two tag heights; Output::reserves_bottom derives 'a bar holds this edge' from the usable area; WindowService::has_frame is false for fullscreen and for a maximized window on an output that reserves its bottom, so the shell's bar carries those controls and the compositor draws the tags again when no zone is claimed. Compositor chrome: layout::control_tags/control_tag_at (the former band_buttons, verbatim) and layout::name_tag (left end, up to TAG_GAP before the first control, capped at NAME_TAG_MAX_WIDTH); collect_name_tag and collect_control_tags replace collect_band and collect_grip and bail when !has_frame. Input: Affordance::Tag replaces Band, Grip is gone, the gap between the tags falls through to the window beneath, edges and corners resize as before. window_groups::tag_drop_target hit-tests the name tag only. COMPOSITOR.md's band rows describe tags. Also: on_outputs_changed's repairs now configure every repaired window through space_sync::apply_resized_geometry, not X11 alone, so a maximized Wayland client is re-sent its size when the bar appears.

## [Home Field widgets — every missing desktop capability as a tile on the one screen](ACTIVE-WORK.md#home-field-widgets--every-missing-desktop-capability-as-a-tile-on-the-one-screen) `@legeos.work.home-widgets/1`

### Launcher widget — make a cold session able to open its first application

`active` · `@legeos.work.home-widget-launcher/2` · part of `@legeos.work.home-widgets/1`

A launcher widget that lists installed applications, filters as the user types, and launches through Launcher1. This is the single most load-bearing gap: without it a freshly booted session cannot open anything at all, because application tiles are derived from windows that already exist (field_model::merge_apps) and are removed when the last one closes. The inventory is already in the shell — AppIdentity1.ListApps is fetched every three seconds into ShellApp::apps and its only consumer today is a grep for nm-tray — and Launcher1.Launch already works and is already called for the network control and for opening files. The widget itself is small; the prerequisites below are not.

### Drive the compositor's ext-session-lock-v1 so Lifecycle1.Lock stops returning NotSupported

`active` · `@legeos.work.session-lock-client/1` · part of `@legeos.work.home-widgets/1`

Make locking the session actually lock it. The compositor implements ext-session-lock-v1 in full (compositor/lege-comp/src/session_lock.rs) and ADR-0010 makes the lock screen compositor-owned, "one provider by construction". What has never existed is anything that drives it: no client calls lock(), so there is no lock surface and no lock. Lifecycle1.Lock is declared with the interface shape settled and returns NotSupported rather than reporting a success it did not achieve.

## [Make LegeOS bootable on the reference laptop and able to build itself, so Lubuntu can be deleted](ACTIVE-WORK.md#make-legeos-bootable-on-the-reference-laptop-and-able-to-build-itself-so-lubuntu-can-be-deleted) `@legeos.work.self-hosting-legeos/1`

### The installation medium does not strand its owner — hardware inventory, seeds that cover it, a live preflight, rescue boot entries and the first ISO build

`active` · `@legeos.work.iso-hardware-safety/2` · part of `@legeos.work.self-hosting-legeos/1`

Answer "will the ISO leave me without video or networking" before a USB stick is written, not after. Four parts: an inventory of the reference laptop joined to the package that provides each module and each firmware file on the base the medium is built from; the seeds carrying the hardware packages that only a Recommends would otherwise pull in; a live preflight (lege doctor --preflight) that the medium runs at boot and that legeos-install refuses to write over; and two rescue boot entries on the medium for the two ways a machine fails to reach a session.

**Acceptance** — 1 of 6 satisfied

## Unparented

### Ubuntu-derived full distribution and latest-stable kernel roadmap

`proposed` · `@legeos.work.full-distribution-roadmap/1`

Turn the LegeOS desktop/session and existing distro scaffold into a supportable amd64 Ubuntu 26.04
binary derivative: clean source builds, signed overlay archive, reproducible image and live installer,
safe in-series updates, recovery, security operations, hardware qualification, and a LegeOS-owned
latest-qualified-stable kernel lane. Linux release candidates remain experimental and Ubuntu's signed
GA kernel remains a rescue path until the independent kernel/driver/signing pipeline is proven.
